claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The starting alloy exhibits balanced strength and fatigue performance.
Grain-boundary diffusion of Al and Cr drives formation of a thin protective oxide layer in the fcc matrix.
The thin oxide layer limits further elevated-temperature degradation.
Under oxidizing conditions, selective oxidation along grain boundaries produces an adherent alumina/chromia scale.
The alumina/chromia scale preserves the alloy's bulk mechanical integrity.
Under reducing conditions, the protective oxide scale is absent or partially reduced.
Absence or partial reduction of the scale increases intergranular degradation.
Temperatures of approximately 700–900 °C are sufficient to activate the proposed grain-boundary diffusion.
Grain-boundary regions become enriched in Al and Cr and consequently undergo local oxidation.
Al and Cr diffusion in oxidizing atmospheres forms a thin, adherent barrier scale that suppresses further oxidation.
Diminished passivation under reducing conditions causes accelerated oxidation at exposed sites.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a stable, thin grain-boundary oxide scale with minimal loss of mechanical integrity relative to the starting alloy.
Reducing exposure will produce less-developed or disrupted oxide scales and more intergranular degradation than oxidizing exposure.
The greater intergranular degradation under reducing exposure may correlate with reduced mechanical performance over time.
Substantially longer exposures may cause phase readjustments and introduce additional degradation mechanisms.
Ti, Co, Fe, and Ni may modulate the oxidation kinetics.
